newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natgas producers boost efficiency in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natgas producers boost efficiency in 1996.

text.p: U.S. natural gas producers boosted efficiency at their fields in 1996, increasing capacity use and maximum feasible capacity, the Natural Gas Supply Association said Wednesday.

The percentage of production field assets used to deliver gas to the transmission pipelines rose to 95 percent in 1996 from 94 percent the previous year, according to NGSA's annual deliverability survey.
The results were based on responses from companies that account for 59 percent of total natural gas production in the lower 48 states.

The growth in capacity utilization came at a time when respondents to the survey increase the amount of production capacity connected to pipelines by 2.7 percent to 31,083 million cubic feet per day at the end of 1996.
"The greater your utilization of your assets, the lower your costs of producing," said Phil Budzik, NGSA's technical analysis director.

Producers' estimates of maximum feasible capacity at their fields jumped two percentage points to 96.6 percent, which Budzik said reflected technological changes which have improved reliability of production facilities.

"A host of technologies have been brought to bear," he said, pointing to new technologies that have limited the need for frequent well workovers, and anti-freeze measures now being used widely around Gulf facilities to prevent production shutdowns during severe winter conditions.
